key_insight: PINN-LPCDD learns medium interfaces while using separate neural networks to preserve sharp contact discontinuities in compressible multi-medium flows.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets shock-driven flows across dissimilar media, including high-pressure-ratio cases with large differences in material stiffness.
method: Use medium-specific subnetworks and learnable interface positions for physically consistent domain decomposition.
Solve Euler equations with artificial viscosity to improve shock-handling robustness.
Exploit Euler-equation scaling invariance to address high pressure ratios.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests on air–air, air–helium, air–water, and air–R22 problems show acceptable accuracy according to the abstract, which provides no quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: Artificial-viscosity tuning and interface-learning stability warrant validation beyond the reported test cases.
paper_title: PINN-LPCDD: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition for Compressible Multi-Medium Flows
